frontline_communication.snippet:
Car 2014 Camaro - I’ve been coming to this location for several years. In August 2025, I had a rack and pinion installed. In March 2026, I brought my car back because I was experiencing a vibration during acceleration. My check engine light was on, and they recommended repairs based on the codes, along with new tires—totaling about $5,000. At no point did they mention that my spindles were cracked.

I had the check engine issues addressed elsewhere (spark plugs and fuel injectors), but two months later, the vibration was still there. I then took my car to Tire Plus, a sister company, and they advised me to return to Firestone, saying the spindle issue might be covered under the warranty from the rack and pinion installation.

When I returned to Firestone, the experience was noticeably different. The store manager, Chrismary, who is usually friendly, barely greeted me. When I explained what Tire Plus had told me, her immediate response was dismissive: “I don’t know why they would tell you to come back here.” She also said that since the car had been driven 11,000 miles, they couldn’t determine when the damage occurred. The mechanic briefly reviewed photos and echoed the same uncertainty.

This was frustrating, especially since the mechanic at Tire Plus indicated the car showed no signs of an accident and believed the issue was likely related to the earlier rack and pinion installation. Chrismary then told me they couldn’t look at the car that day and asked me to return the next day, but didn’t offer to schedule an appointment or provide any clear next steps regarding the warranty.

Overall, I felt the situation was handled with little effort or willingness to investigate. When I’ve paid for services in the past, Chrismary was very friendly. This time, when I raised a potential warranty concern, the response felt dismissive from the start. I would recommend proceeding with caution.

Forgot the mention that Tire Plus felt that Firestone should stand behind the warranty repair so strongly that they did not charge me for the diagnostics test.  They did it for free once they seen what the issue was.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer raised a specific warranty concern and it was dismissed rather than investigated.
frontline_communication.quote: the response felt dismissive from the start

I got a brand new AC unit installed indoors as well as the unit outside. ACS charged over $15,000 total for all the work they did. When it does, it is not powerful at all, the unit is extremely loud (see attached video) and wakes us up in the middle of the night, the temperature is not as cold as it is supposed to be, and it takes more than 4-5 hours to drop only 4 degrees. They sent technicians to my house 8 times, and replaced 4 or more parts over the course of their visits. During the third visit, they had to cut the pipes again so that they could blow out a blockage. A bunch of oil came out of the brand new pipe. After the eighth visit, it still does not work properly, and still makes EXTREMELY loud noises. I called the company and told them that I want a completely new unit. They told me that as long as it eventually reaches the temperature, that they will not replace the unit. They said it doesn't matter how long it takes. Also, they were going to charge me to have another technician come and take another look at it. This company is ridiculous. They respond to this review saying they will come out again. Yeah, and charge more money to fix a busted unit that they gave me. Do yourself a favor and stay away.

Update: The outside unit is dead and no longer turns on. We called to have it looked at, and he said that since the temperature is currently what it was set at when we called, it's normal. frontline_communication.snippet: June 2025, my 72 year old wife needs a new catalytic converter on her 2001 Acura Integra which had 112K miles and she is the original owner.  Dumb me thinks that instead of taking it to our regular mechanic I should go to someone who I think specializes in exhausts, as if the chains that did that 40 years ago still do so today.  I look for Midas, there are none near me.  Then I look for Meineke, I find this one 5 min. from home that I pass by a couple times a week but never saw.  They give me a quote, I pay for the special order part, and come back a week later for install.  The job is done, I start the car, and it is LOUD!  I go back in the office to discuss, they have me sit for about 10 minutes, tell me a O2 sensor cap was left off, but what is now is how it will be.  It is still LOUD!  I take the car home, kicking myself that I let these guys turn my wife’s quiet car into a hot rod.  She sees what was done and she is pissed.  Not only is it LOUD!, but the floor vibrates so that you feel it in your feet on the floor and in your butt on the seat when accelerating.  She is not happy, and I hear it every time she drives.  Now it is March 2026.  The car goes to the regular mechanic for maintenance and he tells me that there is a crack where the catalytic converter meets the mid exhaust pipe and both need to be replaced.  The price he gives me for the catalytic converter is less than half of what Meineke charged.  Add in a new mid pipe and the parts charge is still much less than what Meineke charged tor just the catalytic converter.  And his labor time charge to replace the two parts was the same as the Meineke time charge for one part.  And when I drive away the car is as quiet as when it was brand new.  I cannot prove that Meineke installed a defective part, or more likely damaged the part and the pipe when they did the install.  But as the car was LOUD! from the start and quiet as soon as the cracked parts were replaced it sure seems that way.  And their parts charge is more than double!  I won’t be back there.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer raised the specific complaint that the car was loud after the repair and staff dismissed it as final.

booking_friction.snippet:
If I could give zero stars I would. My family has been living through an absolute nightmare after hiring Frank Gay Services (Lakeland office) for a whole-house repipe and bathroom remodel that started late October now still unfinished December 2025. What was supposed to be a routine job has turned into tens of thousands of dollars in damage, lies from management, and a home that is still not fully functional or safe. Frank Gay has refused to offer any reasonable resolution and now completely backing out of responsibility.
Here are just some of the major issues their crews left behind over the course of the job:
Exterior
• Corroded copper pipe left in the yard; our dogs got to it and scattered pieces everywhere.
Laundry Room / Guest Bathroom
• Brand-new vanity installed with an extra hole cut too high– tech said “just cover it with the toilet paper holder”
• Broken vanity door on a brand-new vanity
• Vanity leaked immediately after install, flooding the laundry room
• Pipes left completely exposed (new plumber said they could and should have been hidden)
• Vanity installed blocking the doorway (new plumber showed multiple ways it could have been flush against the wall)
Kitchen
• Fridge and dishwasher water lines cut for no reason
• Kitchen vent pipe left 2 inches outside the studs, uninsulated and unsealed – forced us to lose cabinet space with an unwanted build-out
• Hot water to kitchen sink still not reconnected
Promised a garbage disposal that I don’t have.
Left side of sink has no piping still
Living Room & Bedroom
• Random cuts in terrazzo floors
• Large gashes and unnecessary holes in walls – outlined in Sharpie to be repaired, then just patched over (Sharpie still visible)
• Crew knocked over a jar containing our recently deceased cat’s fur – glass and fur scattered across bedroom floor no remarked made.
Master Bathroom (the worst of it)
• No caulk around shower or toilet
• Shower installed covering a window without disclosure; not up to code
• Wrong pipes used – new plumber had to rip everything out and replace with correct copper
• Shower pan improperly installed over uneven concrete; leaked immediately
• No pressure test or inspection ever performed (they falsely claimed it “passed with flying colors”)
• On the reinstall day, Frank Gay tech showed up, said measurements were off, the pan was too big, he didn’t have materials, and left – after the old shower had already been demolished
Drywall & Scheduling Chaos
• Drywall crew had no idea of the scope, left at 2 p.m. saying they had a long drive home
• Multiple no-shows, double-booked technicians, and excuses (including being told on Veterans Day that “no one is working”)
• Project manager had no knowledge of our job and asked “How did you even get this number?” when we finally reached him
• Promises made by coordinator “Sarah” were repeatedly broken. She told me work “ was not that bad “
They had to hire an entirely new plumbing company and multiple other contractors to fix Frank Gay’s work. The new plumber has been shocked at the number of code violations and shortcuts taken.
We have photos, videos, texts, and invoices, documenting everything. Frank Gay has stopped responding to us entirely not and will not offer anything beyond a small partial refund that doesn’t even cover a fraction of the damages and delays we’ve gone through. I was told they could not take any money off the job but would offer a water softener and major electrical/hvac work. They’re best and final offer was To do electrical work that I don’t need, and that they claim would be up to $10,000 to change outlets and add light dimmers.
My family has been without a proper working master shower for weeks, living in construction dust and danger. We simply want the public to know what happened so no one else has to go through this. We just want this exposed so no one has to deal with this company.
I attached a few photos over the course of the process of multiple lies and failures.$40,000 and the mess they left behind is unfathomable. Do not use them.
booking_friction.reasoning: Repeated no-shows and double-booked techs show the schedule could not be reliably confirmed.
booking_friction.quote: Multiple no-shows, double-booked technicians

frontline_communication.snippet: Wish I would have read the reviews before I had service done.  Indian Rocks A/C installed my unit originally and I thought they did a good job but what do I know I’m not an a/c person.  The ac recently stopped working and we called and had them come out to do a service on the unit.  They came out a couple days later.  When they started working on the unit I asked if they could do an actual service on the unit because it had not been done in a while and it was full of leaves (that can’t be good for it running very efficiently) they said they would. So a couple minutes later they bring me a small electric box( some sort of capacitor) and try to show me how it’s blackened and melting, I look at it and I don’t see any black from sparks it actually looks fairly new to me just a bit of use on a metal piece down inside. I go ahead and let them change it for $89.  and  I got taken just like the review by Jerry Welch charged $89 for a $9 part.  Then after they where gone (which was only a couple minutes after showing me the part) I took a closer look at the unit and it was still full of leaves.  And I noticed all the wires dangling out the back.  I had similar wires hanging of the unit inside the house. I looked at some of my neighbors units and none had wires exposed.  I called the company to complain, explained to lady my issue and she told me I would have to call back another day.  Well I will not be calling them back for anything.  Would not recommend this company.

frontline_communication.snippet:
We subscribed to Mason’s maintenance membership for AC, plumbing, and electrical at our vacation home, and were pretty disappointed. After each inspection, we kept getting upsell estimates for thousands of dollars.

The last visit was for AC maintenance. The report wasn’t very clear—lots of boxes checked but no detail on what was actually done. When we called, we were assured that the AC lines were drained and the filter was replaced. Five days later, we checked and the filter was very dirty and it was obvious it was not replaced during the maintenance visit.

When we followed up, they first said filter replacement isn’t included. After asking to speak to a supervisor (since this is pretty standard and we even left new filters by the unit), they admitted the technician missed it. But instead of offering any refund for a job that wasn’t complete, they offered a free year of maintenance and asked us not to cancel.

We declined. If they can miss something as basic as replacing a dirty filter, it’s hard for us to trust them with the whole AC system.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Service report gave no usable detail on work performed, and staff later contradicted what they had assured on the phone.
frontline_communication.quote: The report wasn’t very clear—lots of boxes checked but no detail on what was actually done.

delivery_quality.snippet:
My experience with Bill Laursen Construction was extremely disappointing. The quality of workmanship was poor, and much of the work appeared rushed and incomplete. I documented numerous issues with photos throughout the project.

One of my biggest concerns was finding mold-damaged areas being covered over rather than properly remediated. I have photographs showing the condition before it was covered. Homeowners should pay close attention to what is behind the finished surfaces and ask questions before drywall is installed.

I also discovered work being performed without permits where permits should have been obtained. I verified this through local permit records. Homeowners should independently confirm permit requirements and ensure all necessary permits are pulled before work begins.

Communication and scheduling were ongoing problems. There were repeated delays, confusion about project details, and responsibility was often shifted to office staff rather than issues being addressed directly.

I was also concerned by crew members performing electrical and plumbing work that did not appear to be within their expertise. As someone familiar with construction, the work raised serious concerns about quality and professionalism.

Overall, I would not hire this company again. I recommend that anyone considering them thoroughly review all work, verify permits, and inspect completed projects carefully before making final payment.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I am giving two stars only because the work was completed; however, the lack of professionalism and the extreme price point make this service poor value for money. For a total of $4,972.80, one would expect "white glove" service, yet the experience was far from it.

Our initial quote from Ducts All Done for AC cleaning, duct cleaning, and a UV light replacement was a staggering $6,800. For a home with only nine ducts, this was an immediate red flag. After I presented a competitor’s quote of $4,800, the company abruptly matched it. However, subsequent research reveals that for a home of this size, even $2,000 would be considered the high end of market rates. As a first-time homeowner, I was unfortunately unaware that I was being charged more than double the standard rate.

At a premium price point of $5,000, you expect a high level of preparation. Instead, the technicians arrived in an unmarked vehicle and lacked basic professional equipment, including a shop vac, drop cloths, and ceiling repair tools. The job was rushed through in just a few hours, leaving the house a mess and failing to repair the popcorn ceiling where the vents were damaged.

Despite speaking with the owner, we were unable to reach a resolution. If you are paying five-star prices, you should receive five-star service and equipment. Based on the lack of professional standards and the inflated pricing, I cannot recommend this company. Please do your research on market rates before booking.

Note: I am also hiring an inspector to verify that the work was completed correctly.

First, their office person tells me they can’t check the portal where people are entering service call information because she’s the only one that does it and she was out sick. That’s why it took them three days to get to my house. Then the tech tells me I need new coils, that my coils are leaking. billing_or_intake_errors.snippet: I truly hate leaving bad reviews but as a local realtor I like to always give my honest opinion. I’ve used tons of companies to do multiple quotes for properties & never got charged. This company would not let me make the appointment because I was not the home owner or listing agent, I was the buyers agent. Finally the listing agent or seller made the appointment & this company charged me over $100 to come to a property, watch a sewer scope video that the inspector gave us from the inspection that was done, stood in driveway for 5 mins & then left. They took a week to even get me an estimate & then freaki my charged me. I could have emailed the video to them like I did for 3 other companies & received free quotes. But no they said they had to come to the property. On top of it the property isn’t even mine, as I said I’m the buyers agent. Then they threatened to report it to my credit & lower my credit score if I didn’t pay the bill for the property I didn’t even own. So as a realtor, this company is not on my vendor list I give out to all my buyers & sellers because I don’t want this to happen to any of my clients. I hate bad reviews but along with the good comes the ugly & you need to always know both sides of every company.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Customer was billed over $100 for what other vendors provide as a free quote visit, then threatened with credit reporting over the unexpected charge.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: this company charged me over $100 to come to a property, watch a sewer scope video that the inspector gave us from the inspection that was done, stood in driveway for 5 mins & then left.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
Asked for 24 hour service because my husband had just died suddenly, AC was out, and I had people arriving within a few days, most of them elderly, in their 80s. On a unit they installed a year and a half ago (for $15,000). They did not come in 24 hours. Took days for them to get a part. Then promise to fix it the next morning (now day 4). They did not come until 5 pm when I was due at a dinner for me; had to miss it. Six hours later at 11 pm, the repair which was supposed to take 45 minutes was not repaired. Tech said he did not know why. I had requested someone experienced to come to the site, but no one came. Called customer service and they said a supervisor needed to come to the site. Supervisor never came, decided to guide this inexperienced tech through the job, for hours. In the middle of which i talked to the supervisor on the tech's phone, (on speaker phone) and he yelled at me and accused me of "grabbing" the tech's phone - I did not, I was standing there. The ech was polite and trying his best, but he could not fox it. An hour later, he left, saying he could not fix it.

2 customer service women were polite and kind, but 2 others treated me with disrespect (because I had been upset that they gave me no priority which they promised repeatedly at first.) Every time you call this company, you get a different person. The techs vary: some are very good, others are inexperienced.

Also, they use variable pricing. Use lots of salesman tricks, but the worst is that they try to charge exorbitant prices if u live in a nice neighborhood. When I called the manager on it (on a previous repair, a routine cleaning of a clog) because I knew what it should cost, they did bring down the charge - to 1/3 the price they had on the original bill.

Beware. They are not managing their employees well, and I have never experienced this kind of rudeness, and in one situation, downright hostility, by any service company - I have never written a critical comment about any company before this.

This company is out of control, has numerous problematic or inexperienced employees, seems to farm out customer service calls, so those reps have no power at all, has unethical pricing and has no concept of treating customers well to further business. They were cold, heartless and mean in the days after I lost my husband after 43 years marriage. They just did not care enough to try to do a good job.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Non-transparent pricing that varied by neighborhood and dropped to a third of the original bill when challenged.
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: Also, they use variable pricing. Use lots of salesman tricks, but the worst is that they try to charge exorbitant prices if u live in a nice neighborhood.

I scheduled an appointment for a diagnostic due to the check engine light being on for Wednesday, 4/23. On Sunday, 4/20, the car was towed there due to not starting. Someone from Rob called on Monday and said they found the issue was the starter went out. I gave approval to work on it. They completed the car on late Tuesday, but I requested to pick up on Thursday. The cost was $750. Now, the check engine light is still on and the car still has issues starting.

I called back and spoke to Rob. He pretended to be oblivious to the fact that if the car was already there it would make sense to complete the appointment for the diagnostic. He claims the $750 did not include the diagnostic. He said the starter is different than a diagnostic. He advised me that he no longer wants to work on my car because I advised that I could not understand how the diagnostic was not completed, and now (4/26) the starter is having issues.

Now, I have a dysfunctional starter with a warranty and he is refusing to fix it.

I was never rude, my voice tone and inflection was normal, and he was adamant that he would not correct the issue because he did not want to take responsibility.

I want to warn everyone about this place. It is not a reputable company and they are taking advantage and charging excessively and not fixing the issues!

frontline_communication.snippet:
CDS Plumbing is a nightmare. Be ready to manage your own project, check their progress, and call many times wondering why they are destroying your house. While they replaced our sewage line and it works, everything else was disastrous.

I have much more to share and extensive video evidence showing their complete disregard for our home, but Google Reviews won’t accept videos and has a maximum character count which I clearly met.

What they did right:
- Replaced the entire sewage line at a fair price.
- Plumbing has worked so far.

What went wrong:
- Workers left doors/windows open with the A/C running.
- Trash and debris were left everywhere; we had to clean it ourselves.
- Cracked bathroom tiles.
- Dirt and debris from floor work piled onto living room floors with no protection.
- Concrete splattered on baseboards and flooring, causing permanent damage.

The concrete work after plumbing was done by a different company. It was so uneven that floors and laundry room couldn’t be finished. CDS “fixed” it by bringing the same company back, who sanded everything with zero protection. Our entire home was coated in concrete dust on ALL surfaces—furniture, vents, cabinets, clothes, dishes, pantry items, you name it.

Cleanup was brutal. Six family members spent four full days moving out our home, cleaning everything off-site, laundering clothes and bedding, and washing dishes elsewhere. CDS only sent 4–5 cleaners who were reluctant and limited; the cleaning company confirmed CDS minimized staff and refused additional help.

After moving back in, concrete dust continued to come through our air vents and settle on our belongings. Given that I have two children, I requested professional air duct cleaning due to health concerns. The owner was again rude and reluctant.

We never asked for reimbursement for housing, utility costs, or the extra week displaced. Even so, CDS resisted. Dust continued to come through vents, forcing professional air duct cleaning for health reasons. The owner was rude, dismissive, and at one point said he would “not spend another penny,” showing zero concern for our safety or family.

Additional issues:
- A worker failed to reconnect a pipe, flooding our laundry room.
- Bathroom vanity measured incorrectly and is off-center.
- Laundry room vanity installed at an angle; sink leans forward and won’t drain.
- I repeatedly had to inspect the home and property to find unfinished work and leftover debris, requiring multiple return visits.
- Workers smoked marijuana in our backyard twice.

Final thoughts:
Plumbing works, but everything else was handled with zero professionalism. Damage to our home, unsafe conditions, poor workmanship, and dismissive ownership made this extremely stressful. Avoid CDS Plumbing if you value your home, health, or peace of mind.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Very disappointing experience with Air O Force 1. This is a brand-new building with a brand-new AC system, and from the beginning, the experience has been nothing but frustrating. Their plans were poorly thought out, and the thermostat placement was completely incorrect, which caused major issues with airflow — some areas were too hot, while others were freezing cold.

Despite the system being new, they refused to honor their warranty when problems arose. Communication was absolutely horrible — hard to reach, slow to respond, and no accountability. As a business startup, this caused serious disruption, and I was forced to pay out of pocket to correct mistakes that were clearly their responsibility.

They do not stand behind their work, and I would not recommend them to anyone. If you’re opening a business, avoid the headache and go with a company that actually cares about doing the job right and supporting their customers.

in response for the owner answer
After leaving my honest review based on our firsthand experience with this company, I received a defensive public response — and within a short time, the office manager who wrote that response also left a 1-star review on my business page, followed by additional 1-star reviews from what appear to be friends and relatives, none of whom have ever interacted with my business in any capacity.

This kind of retaliatory behavior is deeply unprofessional and speaks volumes about the company's approach to handling customer feedback. My review reflects the real challenges we faced with poor communication, unresolved HVAC issues, and the burden of having to correct problems out-of-pocket in a brand-new commercial building.

I have no issue with companies standing by their work — but retaliating by attacking someone else’s business and reputation is unacceptable. I believe others deserve to know who they are dealing with when choosing a contractor. Businesses should be able to take responsibility, not resort to coordinated online attacks.

We continue to stand by our original review and hope this serves as a reminder to always look beyond the surface when evaluating service providers.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Reviewer explicitly names communication breakdown and unresponsiveness, but the complaint is about reachability/responsiveness rather than rudeness, unclear info, or a dismissed concern, so no listed sub fits.

frontline_communication.snippet: Tyler called to say he would be there at 430pm and did show up at that time. He did clean some of the the mold out. There was a burn smell coming out of the vents on heat, cool and fan cycles after he was done cleaning that was not there before. He said it was probably nothing to worry about. Unfortunately the smell has continued and has gotten worse. It was making us sick so we had to turn off the air conditioner and do without it for days until a professional HVAC tech could come. The HVAC tech checked the air handler thoroughly and found that the UV light installed was defective and causing the problem. He took the unit out.  He expressed shock that Tyler did not follow up at the time of the visit to check the burn smell. After explaining it to Maya from Ductors her response was she would not give us a refund unless we put in a 5 star review in first and that we could keep the unit and sell it. Neither her or Tyler showed concern for what we went through, just wanted the review down. In all conscience we could not sell the light to another person who would suffer as well and we could not put up a 5 star review that was not earned. We are out $752.25 but we still have our integrity. We are pursuing other avenues to  get the money back.
